speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment, can you confirm the baby's gestational age at birth and whether they are the firstborn in the family?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That family history of pyloric stenosis is interesting, but given the bilious nature of the vomiting, we must rule out midgut obstruction first. Has the baby passed any meconium, and is there any abdominal distension or tenderness?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The abdominal X-ray shows a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia. The "double bubble" sign on the X-ray, combined with bilious vomiting and a history of polyhydramnios (suggested by missed checkups), confirms this diagnosis. I do not need any further questions; the imaging is definitive.
